label: Health history findings
blurb: Findings raised from health-history answers. These are conversation priorities, not risk points — nothing in this file affects any risk score.
adaptation: Tiers describe how soon a finding is worth discussing with a clinician, not how urgent care is. The application does not triage, diagnose, or recommend treatment. A finding fires only on an explicit 'yes'; 'not sure' and unanswered never fire.

tiers.label: Discuss promptly
tiers.meaning: Raise this at the start of the next conversation with a clinician.

tiers.label: Discuss soon
tiers.meaning: Worth a dedicated conversation rather than waiting for a routine visit.

tiers.label: Worth mentioning
tiers.meaning: Useful context for a clinician who is already reviewing your history.

single.summary: Chest discomfort in the last 3 months
single.rationale: Chest pain, pressure or tightness is evaluated rather than watched, whatever the estimated risk score says.

single.summary: Unintentional weight loss of 5 kg or more
single.rationale: Losing weight without trying meets published referral thresholds on its own.

single.summary: Episodes of one-sided numbness, weakness or word-finding difficulty
single.rationale: Transient neurological episodes are evaluated promptly even after they have resolved.
Becoming breathless doing things that did not used to cause it is a recognised warning sign.
Vision change has many causes, several of which are worth identifying early.

single.summary: Cancer in a close relative before age 50
single.rationale: Early-onset cancer in a first-degree relative changes what screening may be appropriate.

single.summary: Told you have kidney disease or reduced kidney function
single.rationale: Kidney function affects both cardiovascular risk and how medicines are handled.

single.summary: Previous severe allergic reaction needing emergency treatment
single.rationale: A prior severe reaction is a standing fact that warrants an agreed plan.

single.summary: Three or more courses of antibiotics in 12 months
single.rationale: Repeated infections can point to something underlying rather than bad luck.

single.summary: Drinking above 14 units in a typical week
single.rationale: Above the published low-risk threshold, which none of the three risk models asks about.
Relevant standing history for anyone reviewing your record.

single.summary: Previous blood clot in a leg or lung
single.rationale: Relevant standing history, particularly around surgery and immobility.

single.summary: Stroke in a parent, brother or sister
single.rationale: Family stroke history is context none of the three risk tables records.

single.summary: Kidney failure in a parent, brother or sister
single.rationale: Family kidney failure is a recognised risk context.

single.summary: Unusual tiredness lasting more than two weeks
single.rationale: Non-specific on its own, which is why it sits at the lowest tier; it carries more weight in combination.
The cardiovascular model was chosen because it needs no blood work, so it never sees this.
Associated with both cardiovascular and metabolic risk, and recorded nowhere else here.

single.summary: Known allergy or bad reaction to a medicine
single.rationale: Standing fact worth having on the record before anything is prescribed.

single.summary: Unplanned overnight hospital stay in the last 5 years
single.rationale: Recent unplanned admission is relevant recent history.

combinations.label: C-1
combinations.summary: Chest discomfort together with new breathlessness
combinations.rationale: Breathlessness alone sits a tier lower. Occurring with chest discomfort it is a recognised accompanying feature rather than an independent complaint, so the pair is raised as one finding.

combinations.label: C-2
combinations.summary: Unintentional weight loss together with persistent fatigue
combinations.rationale: Fatigue is deliberately the lowest tier on its own because it is too non-specific to say anything useful about. Paired with unintentional weight loss it stops being non-specific.

combinations.label: C-3
combinations.summary: Recurrent infections together with changed eyesight
combinations.rationale: The combination the risk score cannot see. The diabetes instrument asks nothing about symptoms, so a person can score Low while reporting the pattern most associated with unrecognised high blood glucose.

caveats.short: Estimates first-event risk; a prior event is reported.
caveats.long: This instrument estimates the risk of a FIRST cardiovascular event. A heart attack or stroke has been reported here, which places this person outside the population the model was built for. The score is still shown, and the arithmetic behind it is unchanged, but it does not carry the same meaning it carries for someone without a prior event.
